subject.title: Feature: Distinguish webchat client types (Mac app vs browser)

question: Which WebChat client metadata may agents see, and should it come only from authenticated Gateway connect identity or also from caller-supplied browser/app hints?
rationale: The remaining work crosses the boundary between diagnostic connection metadata and agent-visible context that may affect behavior, so automation should not choose the trust model or permanent API shape.

options.title: Expose trusted Gateway identity only
options.body: Add a typed agent-facing field derived from validated Gateway client info, such as client id/mode/platform, and keep ad hoc hints out of agent authority.

options.title: Allow explicit untrusted hints
options.body: Expose browser/app hints only when clearly marked untrusted and diagnostic, accepting more API complexity to preserve flexibility.

options.title: Keep diagnostics only
options.body: Leave client identity in Gateway logs and do not expose it to agent runtime until a stronger use case or security model is approved.

recommendation.title: Expose trusted Gateway identity only
recommendation.body: Add a typed agent-facing field derived from validated Gateway client info, such as client id/mode/platform, and keep ad hoc hints out of agent authority.

likelyOwner.reason: The most specific unresolved choice is the Gateway auth/security trust boundary for client metadata.
